policy: Sources establish bounded features only. The playable street grid is a stylized, non-georeferenced reconstruction unless a feature is tied to an exact mapped locator. No source image is redistributed by this register.

sources.title: 19th-century plans of Saint Petersburg; Russian National Library Mosaic of Petersburg
sources.verifiedMetadata: RNB describes the detailed 1828 Schubert plan at 1:4200 and lists the 1846 Military Topographic Depot atlas Plans of St Petersburg from 1700 to 1840. The latter is a 1846 publication whose historical map sequence includes the 1840 city state.
sources.pageOrFolio: Catalog and explanatory exhibition pages; individual map sheets/folios must be checked before exact street geometry is claimed.
sources.visualFeature: Macro street and waterway topology; building footprints only where the selected sheet makes them legible.
sources.confidence: HIGH for catalog facts; MEDIUM for macro geography pending sheet-level comparison.
sources.rights: Catalog metadata reviewed; reproduction rights for map images not reviewed. No image reused.
sources.creditedArtist: Military Topographic Depot; Schubert-led survey plan (1828) as attributed by RNB.
sources.gameTransformation: Use as a dated reference for district connections and broad street orientation. Do not use it to claim exact 1847 shop locations or surveyed coordinates without sheet/locator verification.

sources.title: N. I. Tsylov, Atlas of the Thirteen Parts of Saint Petersburg
sources.verifiedMetadata: NEB/NLR catalog records St Petersburg, 1849, 20 leaves and 407 separately paginated plans; held by the Russian National Library.
sources.eraRange: 1849 publication; two years after the game's initial 1847 date
sources.pageOrFolio: Catalog record verified; specific plan folios require separate inspection.
sources.visualFeature: Later street, embankment, lane, state-house, and private-house comparison.
sources.confidence: HIGH for publication metadata; LOW as direct evidence of 1847 conditions.
sources.rights: Catalog metadata reviewed; scan and reproduction rights not reviewed. No image reused.
sources.creditedArtist: Compiled by N. I. Tsylov; individual engraving credits require sheet-level review.
sources.gameTransformation: Comparison only. Never cite the 1849 atlas by itself as proof that a detail existed in 1847.

sources.title: P. S. Ivanov after V. S. Sadovnikov, Panorama of Nevsky Prospect, sunny side, fragment 8
sources.verifiedMetadata: The State Russian Museum catalog identifies a hand-colored lithograph after Sadovnikov watercolors, published by A. M. Prevost in 1835, inventory GR-1929. The museum describes the panorama as a Nevsky street view from the Admiralty to the Fontanka and cautions that some building details came from project drawings for structures not yet completed.
sources.pageOrFolio: Museum catalog object GR-1929, fragment 8; catalog display accessed 2026-11-02.
sources.visualFeature: Facade sequence, carriage traffic, pedestrians, and street-scale visual rhythm for the represented Nevsky frontage only.
sources.confidence: HIGH for the catalog and publication metadata; MEDIUM for interpreting individual architectural details; not direct evidence of 1847 shop occupants or exact game coordinates.
sources.rights: Museum catalog reviewed; image reproduction rights not cleared. No museum image is copied or redistributed.
sources.creditedArtist: P. S. Ivanov, lithographer; after watercolor originals by V. S. Sadovnikov; published by A. M. Prevost.
sources.gameTransformation: Reference only for broad facade rhythm and period street activity. The in-game map stays stylized and non-georeferenced; proposed/unbuilt structures and exact storefront locations are not inferred from this fragment.

sources.title: Ivan Pushkarev, Guide to Saint Petersburg and its Environs
sources.verifiedMetadata: Presidential Library catalog identifies Pushkarev (1808–1848), St Petersburg, 1843, XVI + 468 + 34 pages and one plan; electronic copy source is the Russian State Library.
sources.pageOrFolio: Catalog record only in this pass; page-level guide entries must be read before asserting individual addresses or access rules.
sources.visualFeature: Names of streets, facilities, districts, and visitor routes once page-level entries are checked.
sources.confidence: HIGH for catalog metadata; UNVERIFIED for any specific facility or route not yet read in the scan.
sources.rights: Catalog metadata reviewed; scan access and reproduction terms not reviewed. No scan image reused.
sources.creditedArtist: Ivan Ilyich Pushkarev, author; printer listed by catalog as the Department of Foreign Trade printing house.
sources.gameTransformation: Use only the checked page/entry and locator in the historical feature ledger; do not infer private access from a guidebook listing.

sources.title: Physiology of Petersburg, Part 1, edited by N. Nekrasov
sources.verifiedMetadata: Presidential Library catalog records the 1845 St Petersburg edition, 303 pages with illustrations, and identifies sketches including the Petersburg dvornik, street organ-grinders, Petersburg Side, and Petersburg corners.
sources.locale: Petersburg urban life as portrayed by Russian writers
sources.pageOrFolio: Catalog contents verified; individual scene pages must be checked before paraphrase or quotation.
sources.visualFeature: Literary descriptions of occupations and everyday urban scenes; not a representative city census or unbiased statistical account.
sources.confidence: HIGH for catalog metadata and contents list; MEDIUM/LOW for generalized claims about prevalence.
sources.rights: Catalog metadata reviewed; scan and image reproduction terms not reviewed. No page image reused.
sources.creditedArtist: N. Nekrasov, editor; named contributors as cataloged by the Presidential Library.
sources.gameTransformation: Contextualize fictional daily-life scenes and explicitly label literary representation. Never turn a sketch into a city-wide statistic.

sources.title: Russian Museum virtual exhibition, Saint Petersburg: City and Citizens
sources.verifiedMetadata: The museum lists K. I. Collmann, Hire a Cab (1842, watercolor on paper, inventory R-1099), Ice Delivery (1842, watercolor on paper, R-12703), and Street in the Rain (1840). Museum interpretation discusses ordinary street activity and genre watercolor conventions.
sources.pageOrFolio: Museum object records R-1099 and R-12703; dimensions and media shown on exhibition listing.
sources.visualFeature: Cab hire, ice delivery, street commerce, transport, clothing silhouettes, and rainy street atmosphere.
sources.confidence: HIGH for museum catalog metadata; visual interpretation remains subject to inspecting each original image.
sources.rights: Museum listing reviewed; reuse/download rights not established. Use only as research reference; do not redistribute museum images.
sources.creditedArtist: K. I. Collmann for the two 1842 watercolors; the museum identifies the 1840 Street in the Rain under the same exhibition listing.
sources.gameTransformation: Create original pixel art inspired by visible, inspected features and mark it CUSTOM_ASSET_INSPIRED_BY_PERIOD_SOURCE. Do not claim the pixel reconstruction is a documentary image.

verifiedLimits: The game map grid remains stylized and not georeferenced; map sources do not authorize exact in-game coordinates without a sheet-level comparison.
The 1849 Tsylov atlas is later reference material for the 1847 opening and is not direct 1847 evidence.
Physiology of Petersburg is a literary sketch collection, not a representative statistical survey.
